posts.title: The Product Is Done. Now What? A 30-Day Roadmap for Your First Launch
posts.excerpt: Most builders don't get stuck on the product — they get stuck on the step after shipping. Here's a day-1-to-day-30 market action roadmap.
posts.author: NowBuild Team
posts.content:
You built a tool with AI over the weekend. The landing page is live. You shared it three times — 12 visitors in 7 days, zero signups. That's not a product problem. It's a rhythm problem.

## Why most first launches fall apart

It's not a lack of theory. It's three things compounding: not knowing what today's post should say (blank-page fear), not knowing which channel to bet on (channel paralysis), and posting into silence with no idea whether to continue (the feedback black hole).

## Week 1: Set strategy, publish your first batch

Answer three questions first: How is your product different from the alternatives? Where do your target users already hang out? How much time can you spend daily? Then pick 2–3 core channels and schedule week one's content.

## Week 2: Adjust your message based on reactions

Watch which content gets likes, comments, or DMs. Double down on formats that get reactions; change the angle on ones that don't. This is when you add direct outreach.

## Week 3: Double down on what works

Use day-7 and day-14 data to cut ineffective actions and concentrate your time on channels showing market signal.

## Week 4: Review and decide what's next

By day 30 you should be able to answer: Which channel works for me? Which content structure converts? Next month — go deeper or switch arenas?

## The key isn't perfection — it's rhythm

15–30 minutes a day for 30 days beats one explosive week followed by three silent ones. The market rewards whoever keeps showing up.

posts.title: How to Choose Your First Marketing Channel, by Product Type
posts.excerpt: Product Hunt, Twitter, Reddit, newsletters… too many channels is a first-time marketer's worst enemy. Here's how to subtract.
posts.author: NowBuild Team
posts.content:
The first rule of channel selection: don't pick the hottest one — pick the one your target users are already on. The second rule: at most 2–3 channels in your first month.

## Match channels to your product type

**Tools for consumers**: story-driven posts on visual platforms plus a direct-message funnel. The 'why I built this' side-project story is a natural fit.

**Tools for developers (global)**: build in public on Twitter/X plus a concentrated Product Hunt launch. Accumulate two weeks of content before PH — a cold-start PH launch usually sinks.

**Courses and consulting**: personal network plus long-form newsletters. These products convert on trust; a short conversion path beats broad reach.

**Open source**: README optimization plus a technical community launch. Your README is your landing page — polish it until it's understandable in 3 seconds before promoting anywhere.

## Signals that a channel is working

Within two weeks, look for three things: engagement on content (likes and comments), inbound DMs or link clicks, and at least one real usage or inquiry. All three missing? Consider switching. Any one present? Worth two more weeks.

## The most common mistake

Opening every channel at once. Each channel has its own format and cadence — running five at once means doing all five badly. Subtraction is the most important strategy of a first launch.

posts.title: How to Get Your First 100 Users Without Spending a Dollar on Ads
posts.excerpt: For a first launch, paid ads almost always lose money. Here are three zero-budget paths to your first 100 users.
posts.author: NowBuild Team
posts.content:
The point of your first 100 users isn't revenue — it's market feedback: is your positioning right, does your message land, does the product give people a reason to stay? Running ads at this stage means paying to amplify an unvalidated message.

## Path 1: Tell your own story

'Why I built this' is the highest-performing content in a cold start. Not a feature list — the scene of the problem: what frustrated you, what you tried, why you decided to build. These posts typically get 3–5x the engagement of feature announcements.

## Path 2: One-to-one outreach

List the 20 people most likely to need your product — colleagues, people who asked related questions in communities, users complaining about competitors. Message each one personally and sincerely. No mass blasts. Your first 10 users almost always come this way, and they give the most honest feedback.

## Path 3: Answer questions where users already gather

Reddit, Hacker News, industry Slack and Discord groups — search for the exact problem your product solves, answer thoroughly, and mention your product naturally at the end. One high-quality answer can drive long-tail traffic for months.

## How much time per day

15–30 minutes is enough: one post, or three DMs, or one answered question. What matters is doing it every day for 30 days. Skip three days and your accumulated momentum starts evaporating.

## When to consider paid ads

When you can answer three questions: Which content converts best? Why do users stay? What is one user worth? Until then, keep your money.
